result.title: Rescuing Points Trapped Inside Incorrect Decision Regions: A target for Evaluating and Improving Forward-Forward Learning
result.summary: Forward-Forward learning replaces end-to-end backpropagation with local, layer-wise training objectives. Its variants are evaluated primarily by classification accuracy, often measured with linear probes trained on their representations. We show that this evaluation can over-credit the learning method: a linear probe on the representations of an untrained convolutional neural network already reaches accuracy well above chance. Moreover, a single accuracy value does not reveal which datapoints become correctly classified after training and which remain misclassified. To examine what learning contributes beyond the random, untrained baseline, we present an analysis methodology built on the Boundary Proximity Index (BPI), a multiclass margin normalized by a class-centroid reference. We apply our analysis to seven Forward-Forward variants and related layer-local methods and find that initially misclassified points near the probe's decision boundary generally have higher rescue rates than those farther inside incorrect decision regions. Rescue rates vary substantially across methods, with some correcting a substantial fraction of these deeply embedded points. Together, these analyses offer a way to evaluate representation learning beyond accuracy and identify the rescue of points far inside incorrect decision regions as a target for improving local learning methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出以线性探针准确率评估 Forward-Forward 等层局部学习会高估其贡献——未训练卷积网络的探针已远超随机水平；为此提出以 Boundary Proximity Index（按类质心归一化的多类间隔）逐样本分析七个 Forward-Forward 变体，考察哪些点被训练真正「救回」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「超越准确率、按间隔与质心参照逐样本诊断内部表示增益」的分析范式，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及性能提升是否真来自训练而非探针或先验。
